exposure: maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in the third trimester
outcome: widespread gene expression changes in cord blood mononuclear cells (CBMCs)
upregulation of interferon-stimulated genes in CD14+ monocytes
upregulation of major histocompatibility complex genes in CD14+ monocytes
transcriptional changes suggestive of activation of plasmacytoid dendritic cells
activation and exhaustion of natural killer cells
cohort: Newborns of mothers infected with SARS-CoV-2 in the third trimester (cases) or without SARS-CoV-2 infection (controls) whose cord blood mononuclear cells were analyzed.
finding: Maternal SARS-CoV-2 infection in the third trimester modulates the fetal immune system, even in the absence of vertical transmission, by inducing widespread gene expression changes and T cell clonal expansion in cord blood.
